**Key observations:**
- Microscope (circular field) view of the underside of a leaf
- Multiple raised, brown-orange, granular/crusty pustules scattered across the leaf surface
- Pustules appear to contain spore masses (uredinia) — rough, powdery texture
- Background leaf tissue remains green with clear vein network visible
- Pustules are irregular in distribution, not angular or flat

**Reasoning:**
The raised, granular brown-orange pustules on the underside of the leaf are classic soybean rust uredinia. The knowledge base notes that soybean rust pustules are distinguishable from bacterial pustule (which has lighter-colored, blister-like lesions with a linear crack rather than open spore masses). The brown, grainy spore masses visible here are consistent with rust uredinia rather than any flat lesion disease like Septoria brown spot or frogeye leaf spot.
